questions.stem: A 43-year-old woman with a history of lupus developed a steroid-nonresponsive nephropathy. As a result, she underwent a kidney transplant 1 year ago. She is now on long-term immunosuppressant therapy. Which of the following medications is she most likely taking?
questions.solutionHtml:
Azathioprine
  • The patient must be on a long-term immunosuppressant to decrease the risk of organ rejection after her kidney transplant. Azathioprine is used to reduce the risk of acute graft rejection after kidney transplantation and to treat autoimmune disorders such as glomerulonephritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
  • It interferes with purine nucleotide (adenine, guanine) synthesis and hence DNA synthesis and repair. In the body, hepatic metabolism converts azathioprine to 6-mercaptopurine; the two drugs, therefore, have the same mechanism of action.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old woman who underwent a mastectomy 5 years ago returns to her oncologist for a check-up. She is currently taking exemestane for hormone-responsive breast cancer. What is the normal function of the enzyme targeted by exemestane?
questions.solutionHtml:
Conversion of testosterone to estradiol
  • Exemestane is an aromatase inhibitor, preventing the conversion of testosterone to estradiol and androstenedione to estrone. It works by forming an irreversible bond with aromatase. Two nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitors are anastrozole and letrozole, which inhibit aromatase via reversible competition. It is used to treat postmenopausal women with hormone-responsive breast cancer.
  • It is often used after 2-3 years of tamoxifen treatment, or in patients who have hormone-responsive breast cancer that advances despite tamoxifen treatment. Unlike premenopausal women, for whom estrogen is predominantly synthesized in the ovary, estrogen in postmenopausal women is largely derived from the adrenal gland, where aromatase converts androgens to estrogen


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has a past medical history significant for chronic renal insufficiency. He was recently diagnosed with transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder and will soon begin chemotherapy. Which of the following chemotherapeutic agents should be avoided in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cisplatin
  • Cisplatin is a chemotherapy medication used to treat several cancers. These include testicular cancer, ovarian cancer, cervical cancer, bladder cancer, head and neck cancer, esophageal cancer, lung cancer, mesothelioma, brain tumors, and neuroblastoma. It is given by injection into a vein.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: Among the following side effects, Pulmonary fibrosis is seen with which drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bleomycin

Bleomycin is a medication used to treat cancer. This includes Hodgkin's lymphoma, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, testicular cancer, ovarian cancer, and cervical cancer among others. Typically used with other cancer medications, it can be given intravenously, by injection into a muscle or under the skin.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 927

questions.stem: Among the following options, what Treatment of choice for Hairy cell leukemia is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cladribine

Cladribine is a medication used to treat hairy cell leukemia (leukemic reticuloendotheliosis) and B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia. Cladribine, sold under the brand name Mavenclad, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients.



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Chapter 66, Page No. 1199.

questions.stem: Among the following options, Peripheral neuropathy is caused by which drug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cisplatin

Cisplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a frequent serious dose-dependent adverse event that can determine dosage limitations for cancer treatment. Nephrotoxicity (kidney damage) is the primary dose-limiting side effect and is of major clinical concern. Cisplatin selectively accumulates into the proximal tubule via basolateral-to-apical transport, where it disrupts mitochondrial energetics.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 920

questions.stem: Among the following drugs, which of the following is given orally?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mesna

MESNA: Mercapto Ethane Sulfonic Acid is used to prevent hemorrhagic cystitis from cyclophosphamide. This can be given I.V. as well as orally.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 919, 935

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs is used as a first-line treatment in combination with Ipilimumab to treat metastatic melanoma if the cancer does not have a mutation in BRAF:
questions.solutionHtml:
Nivolumab

Nivolumab is a human IgG4 anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody. Nivolumab works as a checkpoint inhibitor, blocking a signal that would have prevented activated T cells from attacking the cancer, thus allowing the immune system to clear the cancer.



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Chapter 67, Page No. 1221
